hints.title: Bit Count Reduction Steps
hints.text: Notice that after one operation, any number is replaced by its set-bit count, which is at most the string length 800.

hints.title: Precomputing Reducibility
hints.text: Precompute the exact number of operations needed to reduce each count c in [1, len(s)] to 1. A count is valid if it reduces to 1 in at most k - 1 steps.

hints.title: Digit State Tracking
hints.text: Use digit state tracking over the binary string to count strictly positive numbers less than n that produce a valid set-bit count.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: Precomputes reducibility steps for counts up to len(s) and evaluates prefix bit states with memoization.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Binary length up to 800 bits means n can be 2^800, rendering numeric loops completely impossible.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(len(s)^2) memoization table caching bit-index, set-bit count, and tightness flag.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Combines population count reduction step precomputation with binary digit DP.
